Two categories: what's **already in my context** at session start (I don't read these, they're injected), and what I **go read** depending on the task.

## Auto-loaded every session (I never re-read these)

| File | What it gives me |
|---|---|
| `/Users/1curafu/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Your global rules — iOS Simulator for mobile UI, the `simctl` full-path workaround |
| `CLAUDE.md` (repo root) | The architecture record: stack, codebase map, Decisions 1–5, conventions |
| `~/.claude/projects/.../memory/MEMORY.md` | Index of the 12 memory files below (one-line hooks only) |
| claude-mem `$CMEM` digest | Observation IDs from past sessions, fetched on demand |

The 12 memory files themselves (`session-state.md`, `daily-drop-model.md`, `no-ai-attribution.md`, `live-verify-ui-work.md`, `mobile-first-evaluate-at-phone-width.md`, `womens-wardrobe-gap.md`, etc.) are **not** loaded — only their one-line hooks. I read a file only when its hook looks relevant.

## Read before writing code

1. **`docs/STATE.md`** — CLAUDE.md explicitly says "read it first when resuming." Handoff, open points, branch state.
2. **The relevant plan** in `docs/superpowers/plans/todo/` — e.g. for the current branch, `2026-07-24-generator-audit.md`. Plans are the TDD contract.
3. **`docs/superpowers/plans/README.md`** — execution order and which plans block others.
4. **The actual source files** — CLAUDE.md says "when code conflicts with this file, the code is the source of truth."

## Read before UI work (only then)

5. **`PRODUCT.md`** — positioning, brand personality, anti-references, WCAG target
6. **`DESIGN.md`** — The Midnight Atelier: tokens, One Rust Rule, Italic Why Rule, Hairline Rule
7. **`docs/design-system.md`** — the Tailwind implementation side of DESIGN.md

## Read situationally

- **`fitcheck-complete-spec.md`** (at `styling/project/uploads/`) — product vision, DB schema, §7 generation algorithm, §8 routes
- **`docs/BUGS.md`** — before claiming something is a new bug
- **`docs/MONETISATION.md`** — anything touching Pro gating / `lib/outfits/quota.ts`
- **`LOCAL_DEV.md`** — env/Supabase setup problems
- **`docs/superpowers/specs/`** — the design doc behind a plan, when the plan's *why* is unclear
- **`docs/superpowers/plans/scoping/`** — deferred features (packing mode, stylist chat, women's wardrobe)
- **`.superpowers/sdd/task-N-brief.md`** — mid-execution of a subagent-driven plan

**Not read:** `README.md`, `design_handoff_stylist_generator/`, `styling/chats/`, `docs/plans/01–06` (superseded by the `superpowers/plans/` tree), old dated review docs — unless you point me at them.

content.text:
Yes — with one condition attached, because right now the rule would make me *more* wrong, not less.

## Why the rule is sound

The structure already supports it. `docs/STATE.md` is 223 lines, and line 43 draws the fold explicitly:

> _Everything below this line predates 2026-07-22 and describes how the generator first landed — kept for history, but the TL;DR above is current._

So "read lines 9–44, skip the rest" is a real, cheap instruction — not a vague "read the docs." And the TL;DR genuinely carries things the code cannot tell me: that `intent-first-entry` is **superseded**, that real-calendar integration was **rejected** on GDPR grounds, that iCloud `" 2."` duplicates break `npm run build`. I'd rediscover none of those from source, and I'd waste a cycle re-proposing the rejected calendar idea.

## The condition: it's stale right now

```
TL;DR says:  "In flight: smart default occasion — branch feat/smart-default-occasion"
git says:    fix/generator-coverage
Last updated: 2026-07-23  ·  Today: 2026-07-26
```

Three days and five commits of generator-coverage work — plus the open "regenerate doesn't work" investigation — are nowhere in it. If I'd followed your proposed rule this morning, I'd have started from a confidently wrong picture of the in-flight branch. **A mandatory-read file that isn't mandatory-update is worse than no rule**, because it converts "I don't know" into "I know, incorrectly."

So I agree only if the rule is two-sided:

> **Always read the TL;DR section of `docs/STATE.md` before writing any code** — it carries the in-flight branch, superseded plans, rejected approaches, and known-broken things the code cannot tell you. The history below the fold is optional.
>
> **The same obligation runs the other way:** any session that changes branch state, supersedes a plan, or rejects an approach updates the TL;DR before it ends. A stale TL;DR is worse than none — it reads as current. Bump the date on every edit; if the date is more than a few days old, trust `git log` over the TL;DR and say so.

## One limitation worth knowing

`docs/STATE.md` is gitignored (`.gitignore:34` ignores all of `/docs`). That means a subagent I dispatch with `isolation: worktree` gets a clean checkout **without** it — so the rule can't bind subagents, only me in the primary directory. Fine as-is; just don't expect it to propagate. If you ever want it to, the fix is un-ignoring `docs/STATE.md` specifically, which also means it stops being local-only.

Want me to add it to `CLAUDE.md` (under Conventions) and refresh the TL;DR to cover `fix/generator-coverage` and the open regenerate issue in the same pass?

Yes, do both in one pass. Two changes to the rule text first:

Make the staleness check mechanical. "If the date is more than a few days old" is a judgment call you'll evaluate inconsistently. Instead: compare the TL;DR's last-updated date against git log -1 --format=%cd. If commits exist newer than that date, treat the TL;DR as stale — trust git log and git branch --show-current for branch state, and say so explicitly.
Change the update trigger from "before the session ends" to "at the moment it happens." Sessions end abruptly — context runs out, I close the window. An end-of-session obligation is exactly the one that gets skipped, and skipping it is what produced the current staleness. Update the TL;DR when you create the branch, merge the PR, or reject the approach — not later.
Both changes are right — the second especially: the current staleness is itself the evidence that end-of-session obligations don't survive. Let me gather the facts for the TL;DR refresh.
